title: A Constructive High-Speed Crypto-mining Approach with Dual SHA-256 on an FPGA
problem: Bitcoin mining relies on SHA-256 hash throughput. FPGA and ASIC implementations need efficient dual-SHA-256 processing to maximize hash rate and mining profitability.
motivation: Hash rate directly determines mining efficiency and profitability. Improving SHA-256 throughput and power efficiency through parallel processing enables better mining performance on cost-constrained hardware.
method: Dual SHA-256 processing architecture on Virtex-7 FPGA. Compared against various semicustom ASIC architectures at 180nm and 90nm process nodes.
key_novelty: Dual-SHA-256 FPGA implementation achieving 6.09% speedup and 13.40% functional efficiency improvement over standard SHA-256.
contributions: 6.09% speed improvement over standard SHA-256 on Virtex-7 FPGA
ASIC design comparisons at 180nm: 13.67% efficiency improvement
ASIC design comparisons at 90nm: 16.32% efficiency improvement
limitations: Paper focuses on cryptocurrency mining, not mainstream computing. Limited analysis of power consumption. ASIC results are comparative, not absolute metrics.
